snippets.text: ValsAI says Xiaomi open-sourced the RL environments behind MiMo v2.6, and that in two-thirds of the coding tasks the answer is still in the task's Git history, which MiMo finds.
snippets.why: If true, models trained on those environments may learn to look up answers rather than solve problems, a known way RL benchmarks get gamed.

snippets.text: Arena says Jev Router, from Typesafe, does not beat the Pareto frontier on Agent Arena: matching DeepSeek V4.1 Flash costs 38% more with 1.7x the median latency, over 4,700 agentic sessions.
snippets.why: Routers promise cheaper agents by picking the right model per request; Arena's test finds this one mostly picks efficient models but adds cost.

snippets.text: OpenAI's Vaibhav Srivastav says Codex and ChatGPT Work have passed 40 million users, and promises a Banked Reset for subscribers at the end of the day, Pacific time.
snippets.why: It is OpenAI's own user figure for its coding and work products, and the reset suggests usage limits are still a live issue for heavy users.

snippets.text: TestingCatalog says Grok Bot can now search X directly, so one prompt can analyse more than 100 posts, and that its author uses the bot daily to compose an AI brief.
snippets.why: It closes a gap with Grok itself, which already had X search; TestingCatalog's account is its own testing and unconfirmed by xAI.

snippets.text: Pinrail, a Show HN app under the Apache 2.0 licence, gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode a desktop inbox where agents wait for your approval before acting.
snippets.why: It targets the review bottleneck in agent coding; the project is early, with 11 GitHub stars and a README warning of rough edges.

snippets.text: Alibaba Cloud researchers say top-16 shared-vocabulary training keeps at least 96% of full cross-tokenizer distillation gains and beats four baselines, in a paper with 153 upvotes on Hugging Face.
snippets.why: Distilling a model into one with a different tokenizer is a common obstacle; the authors argue that reliable supervision matters more than covering every token.

snippets.text: A paper listed from NVIDIA, UNREAL, reports lifting NoLiMa accuracy at 128K tokens from 1.0% to 24.83% by letting one frozen LLM drop distractors, adding fewer than 500K trainable parameters.
snippets.why: It treats retrieval and long context as one selection problem; the results are the authors' own and no code link is given.
